root_cause.statement: The 500 is not a real grammar violation. Once the JSON structured-output grammar reaches its terminated state (the top-level JSON value is complete), the model is deliberately left UNCONSTRAINED, and it then emits its normal block-terminator special token (Inkling <|end_message|>/<|content_model_end_sampling|>, id 200028). The scheduler still calls grammar.accept_tokens() on that post-termination token; XgrammarGrammar.accept_tokens returns False for an already-terminated matcher, and the scheduler mis-reads that False as a fatal 'grammar rejected tokens' and terminates the request with FINISHED_ERROR -> 500. The bug is the conflation of 'grammar is already complete / nothing left to accept' with 'token was rejected by the grammar'.
root_cause.mechanism: Trace: (1) After reasoning ends, structured output constrains generation to the JSON schema (grammar_bitmask -> apply_grammar_bitmask). (2) When the top-level JSON value completes, xgrammar's matcher.is_terminated() becomes True; XgrammarGrammar._is_terminated is set (backend_xgrammar.py:170,193). (3) On the NEXT bitmask fill, StructuredOutputManager._fill_bitmasks (__init__.py:198-206) sees `apply_bitmask and not grammar.is_terminated()` is False, so it writes the FULL mask (self._full_mask) for that request -> the model is now UNCONSTRAINED. (4) Being an Inkling wrapper-format model, the unconstrained model emits its natural block terminator special token, id 200028 (a dedicated Inkling special token such as <|end_message|> or <|content_model_end_sampling|>), not the EOS the bare JSON grammar knows about. (5) Back in the scheduler (scheduler.py:1829-1855), should_advance(request) is still True (reasoning_ended stays True and should_advance never checks is_terminated), so accept_tokens(req_id,[200028]) is called. (6) accept_tokens (backend_xgrammar.py:152-158) hits `if self._is_terminated: return False` and returns False. (7) scheduler.py:1844-1855 treats False as 'Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [200028] ... Terminating request', sets FINISHED_ERROR -> serving layer returns 500. This exactly matches the symptom: a SINGLE special token (200028) rejected immediately after valid JSON, with the constraint pipeline having already reported 200 OK. The 'above vocab_size / never-allowed token' theory is a symptom-level misread: if generation were still constrained, the bitmask would forbid 200028 and the model could never sample it -- it is samplable precisely because the terminated grammar switched to full-mask.

proposed_fix.summary: Stop treating a terminated grammar as a rejection: do not feed post-termination tokens to accept_tokens. Guard the scheduler's advance call with `not grammar.is_terminated()`, mirroring the identical is_terminated() guards already used on the bitmask-fill path (__init__.py:199 and :324). Once the JSON grammar is complete, the request should keep generating unconstrained and finish through normal stop-token handling, not be killed as a grammar error.

changes.what: At the advance site (~line 1844), add an is_terminated() short-circuit before calling accept_tokens: change `if advance_token_ids and not grammar.accept_tokens(req_id, advance_token_ids):` to `if (advance_token_ids and not grammar.is_terminated() and not grammar.accept_tokens(req_id, advance_token_ids)):`. This skips grammar advancement (and the fatal-error branch) once the grammar has terminated, letting post-JSON wrapper/stop special tokens pass through as unconstrained output.

(Defense-in-depth for spec-decode / multi-token windows where termination happens mid-batch) Harden XgrammarGrammar.accept_tokens: return True (not False) when self._is_terminated at entry, and break out of the token loop as soon as self.matcher.is_terminated() so trailing wrapper tokens after JSON completion are not rejected within a single accept batch. Keep returning False only for a genuine matcher.accept_token() rejection while the grammar is still live.

Scheduler-level regression test: a structured-output (JSON schema) request whose model emits a trailing special token after the JSON completes must finish as FINISHED_STOPPED via normal stop handling, NOT FINISHED_ERROR, and must not log 'grammar rejected tokens'.

considered_second_opinion.why: Round 1: no peer/prior output was named in the step bead (prior_peer_bead empty).

evidence.note: accept_tokens returns False immediately when self._is_terminated (line 158); _is_terminated set from matcher.is_terminated() after processing (170). This False is what the scheduler mis-reads as a rejection.

`if advance_token_ids and not grammar.accept_tokens(...)` -> logs 'Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens %s' and sets RequestStatus.FINISHED_ERROR. No is_terminated() guard here (unlike the bitmask path), so a terminated grammar's False triggers the 500.

_fill_bitmasks writes the FULL mask (self._full_mask) once grammar.is_terminated() is True -> model becomes unconstrained after JSON completes and can freely sample wrapper/stop token 200028. Confirms the disallowed-token theory is wrong.
grammar-advance and bitmask-fill paths already guard with `not grammar.is_terminated()`; the scheduler accept path at 1844 is the asymmetric site missing this guard -- pinpoints the fix.
should_advance returns True whenever reasoning_ended and never checks grammar.is_terminated(), so the scheduler keeps advancing an already-terminated grammar for the post-JSON wrapper token.

Inkling content blocks are wrapped in dedicated special tokens and closed by <|end_message|> or standalone <|content_model_end_sampling|>. After a JSON block the model emits one of these terminators -- the 200028 in the log -- not the bare JSON grammar's EOS.

evidence.ref: bug vllm-vpd log: 'grammar rejected tokens [200028] ... Terminating request' then 500
evidence.note: Exactly one special token rejected right after a valid (200 OK) structured request -- consistent with rejection at the grammar-termination boundary. could_not_verify precise 200028->name mapping without the inkling-small tokenizer, but its role as block terminator is unambiguous from format + single-token symptom.
